newsitem.title: LEBANON: French group blasts Lebanon media law.
newsitem.headline: French group blasts Lebanon media law.

text.p: A Paris-based group that defends press freedom wants French President Jaques Chirac to urge the Lebanese government to reconsider a controversial media law.
"Reporters sans Frontieres asks you to use your influence with the Lebanese authorities to have the broadcasting law revised," the group said in a letter to Chirac, who was expected in Beirut.
The law, which has sparked street demonstrations and strike threats, licensed only four television and 11 radio stations, meaning that scores must shutdown by November 30.

Three of the four licensed television stations are owned by prominent government figures, including Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, while two of the three radio stations allowed to broadcast news bulletins are owned by the same people.
Opposition politicians, the media and union leaders have accused the government of muzzling the media and carving up the lucrative industry among the political establishment.
Chirac will visit Lebanon on the fifth leg of a Middle East tour.
